=== MASTER DIRECTIVE ===
Rebuild the entire HEADERR website visual system, not just the homepage.
Use the existing repository as the source of truth for products, routes, functionality, and assets.
Use Outsiders Store as the primary reference for editorial ecommerce composition and visual rhythm.
Do not clone Outsiders Store code, copy, assets, logos, or proprietary implementation.
Translate the reference principles into an original HEADERR sports-fashion identity.
Do not preserve the current homepage composition merely because it already exists.
Replace generic layouts with image-led editorial compositions.
Preserve working cart, search, wishlist, account, product, checkout, and routing behavior.
Make the result feel like a premium independent sports-fashion retailer.
Do not stop after changing colors or typography.
Do not stop after changing the hero.
Do not stop after changing the header.
Do not use animation to compensate for weak layout.
Treat photography, product merchandising, typography, spacing, and color as one system.
Inspect the entire repository before making major changes.
=== REFERENCE ANALYSIS ===
Open https://www.outsidersstore.com/?ref=land-book.com before implementation.
Open https://jersey-store-five.vercel.app/ before implementation.
Compare header height and density.
Compare navigation hierarchy.
Compare image usage above the fold.
Compare campaign section proportions.
Compare category discovery.
Compare New Arrivals merchandising.
Compare editorial story blocks.
Compare image aspect ratios.
Compare whitespace.
Compare typography hierarchy.
Compare CTA treatment.
Compare newsletter treatment.
Compare footer architecture.
Use the reference for composition and experience, not literal duplication.
=== COLOR SYSTEM ===
Use #50584F as the primary muted olive.
Use #05192F as the primary deep navy.
Use #A59660 as the primary muted gold.
Use #8C7A44 as the bronze accent.
Use #9BA161 as the sage accent.
Use #697B53 as the secondary green.
Use #C68E1D as the amber accent.
Use #AC1A07 as the controlled red accent.
Use #000E39 as the deepest blue.
Do not use all colors equally.
Use #05192F and #000E39 for major dark surfaces.
Use #50584F for muted editorial surfaces.
Use #697B53 and #9BA161 for restrained secondary accents.
Use #A59660 and #8C7A44 for premium metadata and borders.
Use #C68E1D sparingly for important calls to action.
Use #AC1A07 mainly for genuine warnings or very deliberate campaign emphasis.
Do not turn the site red.
Do not introduce unrelated neon colors.
Do not use gradients as the primary visual language.
Create centralized CSS variables for every color.
=== LANDING PAGE ===
Create a long-form editorial retail homepage.
Start with a compact announcement bar.
Follow with an editorial header.
Follow with a full-width image-led campaign hero.
Follow with an asymmetric category discovery composition.
Follow with New Arrivals.
Follow with a major Football campaign.
Follow with Football products.
Follow with a major Cricket campaign.
Follow with Cricket products.
Follow with a Streetwear editorial section.
Follow with a Featured Drop.
Follow with a HEADERR culture story.
Follow with Journal or editorial content when real content exists.
Follow with a newsletter.
Finish with a complete footer.
Do not make every section the same height.
Do not make every section use the same card component.
Alternate image-heavy, product-heavy, dark, light, and text-led sections.
Use visual breathing space between dense merchandising sections.
=== HEADER ===
Use SHOP, FOOTBALL, CRICKET, STREETWEAR, and CULTURE as primary navigation where those routes exist.
Center the HEADERR logo or wordmark.
Place SEARCH, ACCOUNT, WISHLIST, and BAG on the right.
Keep the header compact.
Keep the header visually connected to the hero.
Allow a transparent initial state when the hero supports it.
Transition to a solid deep navy or deepest blue surface while scrolling.
Do not turn the entire page into a white dropdown when navigation opens.
Use consistent horizontal padding.
Use accessible icon buttons.
Keep keyboard focus visible.
Allow Escape to close overlays.
Do not hide essential navigation behind animation.
=== HEADER ANIMATION ===
Fade the header into view on initial load.
Scale the logo from approximately 0.97 to 1.
Reveal navigation items with a 40–70 millisecond stagger.
Reveal utility icons after the primary navigation begins.
Use 400–600 milliseconds for the initial logo reveal.
Use opacity and transform instead of layout properties.
Compress header height subtly on scroll.
Target approximately 76 pixels to 64 pixels on desktop.
Use approximately 300–400 milliseconds for header compression.
Restore header height smoothly when scrolling upward.
Never bounce the logo.
Never rotate the logo.
Never use a continuous idle animation on the header.
=== MEGA MENU ===
Build a compact editorial mega menu rather than a full-screen canvas.
Target approximately 360–440 pixels on desktop.
Open directly beneath the header.
Keep the hero visible around the menu.
Use navigation columns plus three visual image cards when assets allow.
Use real HEADERR assets for the visual cards.
Do not use unrelated stock images.
Switch between Football, Cricket, Streetwear, Culture, and Shop content without closing the menu.
Use real routes only.
Use real product categories only.
Use a pointer tolerance zone so the menu does not close while moving from navigation to content.
Animate opacity from 0 to 1.
Animate vertical position from -8 pixels to 0.
Use 300–450 milliseconds.
Stagger text links by 40–60 milliseconds.
Stagger images by 60–80 milliseconds.
Scale menu images from approximately 1.04 to 1.
Do not bounce the menu.
Do not rotate menu cards.
=== HERO ===
Replace the current generic hero composition.
Use a real HEADERR campaign image, product composition, or video when available.
Make the image the dominant visual element.
Use a restrained campaign label.
Use a large editorial headline.
Use concise supporting copy.
Use one primary CTA.
Use negative space in photography for text.
Use a subtle readability gradient only when necessary.
Do not place a large floating white card over the hero.
Do not create a generic SaaS-style centered hero.
Do not invent campaign claims.
Use actual collection names and actual product data.
Reveal hero image from scale 1.06 to 1.
Fade hero image from 0 to 1.
Use 1200–1600 milliseconds for the hero image.
Reveal label before headline.
Reveal headline before description.
Reveal description before CTA.
Use 60–100 milliseconds between text elements.
Use line clipping for large headlines when appropriate.
Never rotate words.
Never use 3D text.
Never use particle effects.
=== CATEGORY DISCOVERY ===
Do not create three identical category cards.
Create an asymmetric editorial mosaic.
Give Football the dominant visual role.
Give Cricket a strong visual role.
Give Streetwear a fashion-led visual role.
Use real HEADERR imagery.
Use large image areas.
Use small editorial labels.
Use large category names.
Use subtle arrows.
Avoid excessive borders.
Avoid giant rounded corners.
Reveal category blocks on scroll.
Use opacity and translateY for scroll entry.
Stagger entries by approximately 80–120 milliseconds.
Scale imagery from 1 to approximately 1.04 on hover.
Move category text upward 4–6 pixels on hover.
Move arrows 4–6 pixels on hover.
Use 300–450 milliseconds for hover.
Never rotate category imagery.
=== NEW ARRIVALS ===
Build New Arrivals as a serious retail merchandising area.
Use real HEADERR products.
Do not create fake products.
Do not create fake prices.
Do not create fake stock values.
Use four product columns on wide desktop where appropriate.
Use three columns at intermediate widths when necessary.
Use two columns on mobile.
Keep product image ratios consistent.
Keep product metadata minimal.
Display the actual product name.
Display the actual price.
Display edition or category only when useful.
Keep wishlist controls discreet.
Use small image scale on hover.
Target approximately 1.02–1.03 image scale.
Crossfade to a secondary image when one exists.
Use 350–500 milliseconds for image crossfade.
Reveal quick add only when the existing ecommerce logic supports it.
Slide quick add upward 6–10 pixels.
Fade quick add from 0 to 1.
Do not bounce product images.
Do not make cards jump.
=== FOOTBALL ===
Create a major Football editorial campaign.
Use a full-width or dominant image.
Use real Football assets.
Use a strong Football headline.
Use collection metadata only when real.
Highlight Player Version only when real data exists.
Highlight Master Edition only when real data exists.
Use a clear Shop Football CTA.
Use deep navy or deepest blue around the campaign.
Use muted gold for editorial metadata.
Reveal the image with a clip expansion.
Use 800–1000 milliseconds for the image reveal.
Fade text from 0 to 1.
Move text upward 20–30 pixels.
Reveal CTA after headline.
Do not duplicate the exact Cricket composition.
=== CRICKET ===
Give Cricket equal design importance to Football.
Use real Cricket imagery.
Use real Cricket products.
Use a different composition from Football.
Use a text-and-image split when appropriate.
Use a full-width campaign when the asset supports it.
Use sage and olive accents selectively.
Use deep navy for contrast.
Do not treat Cricket as an afterthought.
Do not duplicate Football copy.
Do not duplicate Football layout blindly.
Keep Cricket fashion-oriented.
=== STREETWEAR ===
Treat Streetwear as fashion rather than merchandise.
Use real apparel photography.
Use large negative space.
Use strong editorial typography.
Keep product information restrained.
Avoid scoreboard aesthetics.
Avoid gaming aesthetics.
Use muted olive, navy, sage, and gold around imagery.
Use large editorial image crops.
Use subtle scroll reveals.
=== FEATURED DROP ===
Create a visually dominant Featured Drop.
Use #05192F as a major background.
Use #A59660 as a restrained accent.
Use #AC1A07 only when a genuine emphasis is needed.
Use one dominant image or product composition.
Use a strong collection title.
Use concise supporting copy.
Use one primary CTA.
Reveal image from scale 1.06 to 1.
Reveal headline with a vertical clip.
Reveal CTA after supporting text.
Do not continuously animate the section.
=== EDITORIAL AND CULTURE ===
Use editorial storytelling to interrupt product merchandising.
Use real HEADERR stories and campaigns where available.
Do not fabricate interviews.
Do not fabricate quotes.
Do not fabricate statistics.
Use large images.
Use small editorial labels.
Use strong headlines.
Use concise descriptions.
Use real destinations for Read Story links.
Reveal images with scale 1.03 to 1.
Reveal text from approximately 20 pixels below.
Move editorial arrows approximately 5 pixels on hover.
Do not rotate editorial cards.
=== ASYMMETRIC IMAGE SYSTEM ===
Use more than one image aspect ratio.
Use portrait images for fashion/editorial photography.
Use landscape images for campaigns.
Use square images primarily for product merchandising.
Use one dominant image with smaller supporting images.
Maintain a logical reading order.
Collapse asymmetric layouts intentionally on mobile.
Do not force every image into a square.
Do not create asymmetry that makes navigation confusing.
=== MOTION SYSTEM ===
Create reusable FadeIn, FadeUp, ScaleReveal, ImageReveal, ClipReveal, Stagger, Drawer, MenuReveal, and PageTransition variants.
Use 150–220 milliseconds for micro interactions.
Use 250–350 milliseconds for standard UI.
Use 350–500 milliseconds for drawers and menus.
Use 500–800 milliseconds for ordinary scroll reveals.
Use 700–1000 milliseconds for editorial image reveals.
Use 1200–1600 milliseconds for hero entry.
Prefer cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1).
Use transform and opacity for most animations.
Do not animate top or left continuously.
Do not animate width or height continuously unless required by a drawer.
Do not use random animation timings.
Do not use spring bounce for ordinary UI.
Do not use particle systems.
Do not use 3D rotations.
Do not use excessive blur transitions.
=== REDUCED MOTION ===
Implement prefers-reduced-motion.
Disable heavy parallax when reduced motion is enabled.
Reduce stagger when reduced motion is enabled.
Reduce large transforms when reduced motion is enabled.
Keep essential navigation functional without animation.
Keep simple opacity transitions where appropriate.
=== MOBILE ===
Design mobile intentionally rather than merely stacking desktop.
Use a compact mobile header.
Use Menu, centered logo, and Bag or the existing equivalent.
Use a right-side mobile navigation drawer.
Use accordion navigation.
Use two-column product grids.
Use large editorial images.
Use shorter campaign copy.
Reduce hero typography.
Reduce parallax.
Avoid horizontal overflow.
Use comfortable tap targets.
Do not depend on hover.
Use 350–450 milliseconds for mobile drawer opening.
Stagger navigation items by 40–60 milliseconds.
=== COLLECTIONS ===
Redesign Football collection.
Redesign Cricket collection.
Redesign Streetwear collection.
Redesign New Arrivals collection when it exists.
Use a large editorial collection heading.
Use a real collection image when available.
Use real collection description when available.
Use real filter data.
Use real sorting logic.
Keep filters visually premium.
Avoid dashboard-like filter controls.
Use a clean product grid.
=== FILTERS ===
Use a compact desktop filter bar or sidebar.
Use a mobile filter drawer.
Animate the drawer from the right.
Use approximately 300–400 milliseconds.
Fade the backdrop independently.
Allow Escape to close.
Preserve filter state.
Do not break existing filter logic.
Do not reload unnecessarily.
=== PRODUCT PAGE ===
Redesign the product detail page.
Use a large image gallery.
Use a sticky product information column on desktop where appropriate.
Use swipeable images on mobile.
Display actual title.
Display actual price.
Display actual variants.
Display actual sizes.
Display actual availability.
Display actual specifications.
Do not invent reviews.
Do not invent ratings.
Keep Add to Bag dominant.
Keep Wishlist secondary.
Crossfade gallery images in 300–450 milliseconds.
Use subtle thumbnail transitions.
=== CART SEARCH WISHLIST ACCOUNT ===
Preserve existing cart logic.
Redesign the cart drawer.
Slide cart drawer from the right in 350–450 milliseconds.
Fade the cart backdrop separately.
Prevent body scrolling behind an open drawer.
Preserve quantity controls.
Preserve remove controls.
Preserve checkout behavior.
Redesign search as a premium overlay or drawer.
Use real search results.
Use useful empty search states.
Preserve wishlist persistence.
Use a subtle heart animation under 250 milliseconds.
Redesign account pages without creating a generic dashboard.
Preserve authentication and account data.
=== FOOTER NEWSLETTER ===
Create a premium newsletter section.
Use concise real copy.
Use actual newsletter integration if available.
Do not fake successful subscription.
Validate email input.
Create useful error states.
Use deep navy or olive as the newsletter surface.
Use gold or sage as a restrained accent.
Create a complete footer.
Use only real routes.
Use only real contact and social information.
Do not create dead links.
Keep the footer calm and editorial.
=== ACCESSIBILITY ===
Use semantic HTML.
Use accessible buttons.
Use accessible links.
Use meaningful image alt text.
Use visible keyboard focus.
Use aria-labels for icon-only controls.
Use dialog semantics for overlays.
Trap focus where appropriate.
Restore focus after closing dialogs.
Allow Escape to close overlays.
Maintain sufficient contrast.
=== PERFORMANCE ===
Optimize large images.
Use modern image formats when supported.
Lazy-load below-fold imagery.
Prioritize the hero asset.
Do not load every image immediately.
Avoid unnecessary JavaScript.
Reuse existing animation libraries when available.
Use Intersection Observer for scroll reveals.
Avoid expensive scroll handlers.
Avoid layout thrashing.
=== DATA AND FUNCTIONALITY ===
Use the existing product source of truth.
Do not create a parallel fake product database.
Do not hardcode prices that can become stale.
Do not hardcode stock values.
Do not hardcode reviews.
Do not hardcode customer counts.
Do not hardcode fake campaign statistics.
Preserve existing routes.
Preserve existing product links.
Preserve cart.
Preserve checkout.
Preserve wishlist.
Preserve account.
Preserve search.
=== CODE ARCHITECTURE ===
Create reusable AnnouncementBar.
Create reusable Header.
Create reusable MegaMenu.
Create reusable MobileMenu.
Create reusable SearchOverlay.
Create reusable HeroCampaign.
Create reusable CategoryMosaic.
Create reusable ProductGrid.
Create reusable ProductCard.
Create reusable EditorialCampaign.
Create reusable EditorialStory.
Create reusable Newsletter.
Create reusable Footer.
Create reusable CartDrawer.
Create reusable FilterDrawer.
Create reusable ProductGallery.
Create reusable animation variants.
Do not create one monolithic homepage component.
=== ANTI-PATTERNS ===
Do not make the site look like a generic Shopify template.
Do not make the site look like a sports dashboard.
Do not make the site look like a gaming interface.
Do not use neon cyberpunk styling.
Do not use excessive glassmorphism.
Do not use excessive gradients.
Do not use excessive rounded cards.
Do not use excessive shadows.
Do not use random stock photography.
Do not use unrelated sports imagery.
Do not create fake editorial content.
Do not create fake reviews.
Do not create fake statistics.
Do not leave the old homepage underneath new styling.
Do not compensate for weak composition with excessive animation.

Inspect the complete homepage.
Inspect the first viewport.
Inspect Football.
Inspect Cricket.
Inspect Streetwear.
Inspect New Arrivals.
Inspect at least one product page.
Inspect search.
Inspect cart.
Inspect wishlist.
Inspect account.
Inspect desktop navigation.
Inspect mega menu.
Inspect mobile menu.
Inspect filters.
Inspect add-to-cart.
Inspect wishlist interaction.
Inspect product gallery.
Inspect responsive behavior.
Inspect keyboard behavior.
Inspect reduced motion.
Run the production build.
Fix every build error.
Fix every runtime error.
Remove debug output.

Do not return only recommendations.
Do not return only a design plan.
Implement the redesign directly in the repository.
Inspect the result in a browser.
Iterate after visual inspection.
Compare the finished composition against Outsiders Store's editorial retail principles.
Do not make HEADERR a clone.
Make HEADERR clearly recognizable as its own brand.
Make the visual change obvious from the first viewport.
Make the entire homepage composition substantially different from the current site.
Make the collection pages substantially different from the current site.
Make the product pages substantially different from the current site.
Make the header, menus, search, cart, wishlist, and account feel like one design system.
Preserve the ecommerce engine.
Replace the presentation layer.
Run the final build.
Fix all errors.
Perform final desktop QA.
Perform final tablet QA.
Perform final mobile QA.
Do not declare completion until the redesigned site is actually rendered and functional.
